newsitem.title: USA: Profits seen in Schering veterinary deal.
newsitem.headline: Profits seen in Schering veterinary deal.

text.p: Wall Street analysts predicted Schering-Plough Corp will quickly reap benefits from its planned $405 million purchase of Mallinckrodt Veterinary Inc announced Monday, improving the unit's profit margins significantly by 1998.

"I would expect that Schering would at least double the Mallinckrodt unit's margins next year to 15 percent," said Rodman & Renshaw pharmaceuticals analyst Jim Keeney, who estimated it had 6.5 percent margins in the past year.

"Schering will pull out costs and get rid of duplicative manufacturing and employee expenses," Kenney said, and in the process likely add three to four cents to Schering-Plough's 1998 per-share earnings, he said.
Prior to Monday's announcement, Kenney had estimated earnings of Schering-Plough, based in Madison, N.J., would grow by 15 percent to $4.35 per share by the 1998 fiscal year ending June 30.

Under the deal, Schering said it would pay cash to buy the Mallinckrodt unit and merge it into Schering's smaller animal health operation to form the world's sixth largest animal health business with annual sales of $650 million.
Mallinckrodt Inc, based in St. Louis, makes health care and specialty chemical products. In October 1995 it bought Syntro Corp, which specialized in biotech vaccines for swine.
"This enhances Schering-Plough's distribution in Europe and Asia by a large margin and will be accretive to earnings by next year," said Goldman Sachs pharmaceuticals analyst Prem Lachman.
Lachman said it was difficult to determine exact profit margins at the Mallinckrodt unit, which had worldwide sales of $456 million in 1996.
He pegged them more generously than Keeney -- "in the 10 to 15 percent range."
But Lachman said they were far shy of the 20-percent margins he said Schering has attained in its own animal health unit, which reported sales of $196 million last year.

"You can bet Schering will wring higher profits out of the Mallinckrodt operation," Lachman added. "My guess is they will probably bring its operating margins up to between 15 and 20 percent by 1998."

The Mallinckrodt veterinary unit focuses on parasiticides, growth promotants and biologicals for farm animals, with about 25 percent of sales in the United States, 35 percent in Western Europe, 20 percent in Latin America and 10 percent in Asia.
Mallinckrodt's stock price settled at 36-3/8 on Monday, up 1/4 from last Friday.
Schering's unit concentrates on anti-infectives and biologicals. It's stock finished at 87-1/8, up five-eighths.
